body: As currently defined "link processing options"'s "destination" member can only hold a string, not null. So I think there are several issues here.

> Reopening for [@TimvdLippe](https://github.com/TimvdLippe)'s comments [#11727 (review)](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11727#pullrequestreview-3295467097)

It's not a noop...
It is set for preloads: in https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#link-type-preload:link-options-destination-3 (`<link rel=preload>` element) and in  https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#processing-link-headers:link-options-destination (
preload headers).

It's a noop for other link types but I guess that's expected because they have a fixed destination?

Suggesting to close this @TimvdLippe. The other typo review comment was fixed by an editorial PR.

The no-op is for prefetch specifically, it doesn't use the preload steps as I see it. Will read once more later this week.

Still, the other comment about nullable destination still applies in the linked comment. We had to remove that line to make it work in Servo.

> The no-op is for prefetch specifically, it doesn't use the preload steps as I see it. Will read once more later this week.

It's by design. Prefetch doesn't support the as attribute.
> 
> Still, the other comment about nullable destination still applies in the linked comment. We had to remove that line to make it work in Servo

Is that for prefetch?

Nullable would be the case if translating the preload destination fails, and only for preload. In that case preloading would bail out early.

@TimvdLippe 
Note that the default for [`destination`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#link-options-destination) is now the empty string and not null. Only preloading can set it to `null`. So sounds like you have not changed the default destination to the empty string, as per the spec PR?

https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/39549 is the reason this issue was opened. One of the changes it made was changing `LinkProcessingOptions::destination` from `Option<Destination>` to `Destination`. In other words: before it was nullable, now it isn't.

It is always initialized to `Destination::None` which is the empty string in our case. The cases where `destination` is set to a different value are:

1. https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#apply-link-options-from-parsed-header-attributes where step 1.3 checks for `null`, so `destination` is always non-null. Implemented in Servo here: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/processingoptions.rs#L114-L120
2. https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-preload%3Afetch-and-process-the-linked-resource-2 where step 4 and 5 do the exact same. Implemented in Servo here: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/html/htmllinkelement.rs#L784-L791

Therefore, `LinkProcessingOptions::destination` is always non-null and we adhere to the spec. When we look at usages of `LinkProcessingOptions::destination`, we see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element:link-options-destination Given that it is always non-null (it's the default empty string or it is assigned to an existing value), this check is redundant. It can never be null, so it can never return null in this algorithm. In https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/39549 we there had to remove this line to make it work: see https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/39549#discussion_r2399523070

Then for the assignment of the empty string to `options.destination` in the prefetch link algorithm. The spec is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-prefetch:fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource-2 which Servo implements here: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/html/htmllinkelement.rs#L509-L520 We construct a new `LinkProcessingOptions` per https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#create-link-options-from-element Since step 2 does not set a destination, we initialize it to the empty string: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/html/htmllinkelement.rs#L429 Immediately afterwards in step 3 of prefetch fetching (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-prefetch:link-options-destination) we once again set it to the empty string. Since the object already has that value, I believe that step 3 here is redundant, since it was already set to it when constructing options.

Opened #11757 with the changes as I see it.

> [servo/servo#39549](https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/39549) is the reason this issue was opened. One of the changes it made was changing `LinkProcessingOptions::destination` from `Option<Destination>` to `Destination`. In other words: before it was nullable, now it isn't.

Oh, you're right - there is a bug in the `dfn`, it can still be null (meaning "an invalid `preload` `as attribute).

It can never be null, so it can never return null in this algorithm. It can be null, the type should still be `Option<Destination>`, where nullopt means "invalid".

The spec is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-prefetch:fetch-and-process-the-linked-resource-2 which Servo implements here: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/html/htmllinkelement.rs#L509-L520 We construct a new `LinkProcessingOptions` per https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#create-link-options-from-element Since step 2 does not set a destination, we initialize it to the empty string: https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/5887e1e963faf5eec9c25a0528b4d77a335eb5e3/components/script/dom/html/htmllinkelement.rs#L429 Immediately afterwards in step 3 of prefetch fetching (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-prefetch:link-options-destination) we once again set it to the empty string. Since the object already has that value, I believe that step 3 here is redundant, since it was already set to it when constructing options.

Thanks, commented on the PR.

Where can we assign a `null` value to destination? I think the part you refer to is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#processing-link-headers:link-options-destination where we have the `if rel is "preload"` case, but there we never run step 1.4 if destination is `null`, given that step 1.3. bails out early. The way I check all usages/assignments of destination is by clicking on https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#link-options-destination and I can't find any assignment where the value could be `null`.

The way I check all usages/assignments of destination is by clicking on https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#link-options-destination and I can't find any assignment where the value could be `null`.

Ah you're right, it's a redundant check. So your PR is 100% correct, sorry for misunderstanding (had to refresh my memory from 4 years ago...)
